summary: Requested a permanence measurement for the startup block, whose trigger observations so far are bounded at five seconds and whose permanence argument therefore leans on source reasoning. The harness keeps the boundary pair already used at the default batch size, 8192 and 8193 seeded entries with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, but watches the control for ten seconds and the 129-batch trigger for thirty. A local probe of the corrected harness gave exactly the expected contrast: the control returned in 6 ms while the 129-batch case had not returned after 30 s and still had one goroutine inside processLogs, which makes the window roughly five thousand times longer than a completed replay of the same shape needs. Two comparisons encode the required behaviour, that each constructor return inside its window, with the control expected to hold and the trigger expected to be violated. Case events are emitted before each attempt and result events after it, so the admission prerequisites are anchored to the case record rather than to their own result event. The submission validates with zero schema errors, the harness file exists, and it requests one execution.
